Status: `human_approval_pending`. This is an agent-source-checked candidate machine draft, not approved public copy or a gold benchmark.

Foushee voted against the reviewed proposals to fund federal operations, set a framework for later tax-and-spending legislation, fund military construction and veterans programs, and narrow SBA loan eligibility. She did not vote on a separate SBA rule-cost proposal.

The six substantive Yes-or-No roll calls reduce to four episodes because H.R. 5371 and H.Con.Res. 14 were each voted on at two materially different stages. Foushee voted against both reviewed government-funding stages, both reviewed budget-framework stages, the House military-construction and veterans proposal, and the SBA loan-eligibility proposal. The record contains:

- six substantive Nay votes across four episodes;
- one Not Voting record on H.R. 2965, excluded from support/opposition;
- one source-grounded but nonbinding WIC negotiating instruction, excluded as a procedural control; and
- one mixed seven-amendment package, excluded because no single policy position safely describes it.

The reviewed records show several bounded choices but do not support one coherent Economy & Taxes philosophy. They do not support an ideology label, party-loyalty assessment, motive claim, prediction, or voting recommendation.

- Opposition to both reviewed stages of the 2025 government-funding package: the initial House version and the later Senate-revised package that became law.
- Opposition to both reviewed stages of the FY2025-FY2034 budget framework, which authorized later drafting but did not itself change taxes or benefits.
- Opposition to the reviewed House military construction and veterans funding bill.
- Opposition to the reviewed House bill restricting SBA-backed loan eligibility by specified immigration status.

ten_second.practical_choice: Whether to pass H.R. 27 after the certification amendment failed.

thirty_second.affected: Federal enforcement and research agencies, researchers, defendants, and communities affected by fentanyl-related substances.
thirty_second.mechanism: The bill would make classwide Schedule I treatment permanent and set related penalty and research-registration rules.
thirty_second.prior_baseline: Temporary classwide scheduling for fentanyl-related substances was already in place.
thirty_second.scale_or_timing: This was the House's February version, not the later enacted bill.
thirty_second.what_happened_next: H.R. 27 passed the House but did not itself become law.

two_minute.argument_boundary: The arguments describe the bill-level dispute; they do not identify Foushee's reason for voting Nay.
caveats: H.R. 27 and S. 331 are related but not identical actions.
A Nay does not assign a reason.
two_minute.detail: The vote followed rejection of a proposed overdose-reduction certification condition.
two_minute.later_history: The Senate later sent the House the related S. 331, which became Public Law 119-26.

opponent_argument.argument: Opponents argued that permanent classwide scheduling and associated penalties could repeat harms of earlier drug policy and inadequately distinguish substances.
